set.text:
Nari: I want to buy these headphones. They have 4.8 stars, so they must be great.
Omar: How many reviews are there?
Nari: Only twelve, but they're all very positive.
Omar: That might be a warning sign. A small number of reviews can be unreliable.
Nari: Why? Almost every reviewer gave five stars.
Omar: Exactly. Real opinions usually vary, so perfect scores can mean that the seller wrote some of them.
Nari: I hadn't thought of that. How can I tell?
Omar: Look for detailed reviews with pros and cons, and check whether the dates are all the same.
Nari: Several were posted on the same day. And they all use the word 'amazing'.
Omar: That does look suspicious. Compare them with the reviews of a model that has hundreds, even if its score is only 4.4.
Nari: A lower score from more people might be more honest, then.
Omar: Right. You'd get a truer picture.
